title: Bring judgment closer
standfirst: The most expensive feedback can be the observation that arrives after other work has depended on its absence.

blocks.text: A team can be learning quickly about the wrong question. During the correction window, the studio improved floor clearance and repaired the loaded-model checks. Max still leaned into the press. The numerical result had become more trustworthy before the performance became acceptable. The missing feedback was not another description of the intended motion; it was the motion itself.

The surrounding tools, execution environment and records are often called an agent’s harness. They determine what the model can inspect, what it can change and what feedback returns. Context engineering then decides which of those observations, instructions and past results reach the next decision. These are parts of the reasoning system, even when they contain no learned parameters.

blocks.alt: Retained R10 departure capture: large facade surfaces obscure almost the entire factory view while the controls and End of shift label remain visible.
blocks.caption: Retained R10 departure view, published with the 25 October materials. This complete frame shows what the browser delivered at one instant; it cannot establish how long the obstruction lasted.

blocks.text: There is a day’s work behind this wall. The action history can tell us who left the factory. The view gives us stone, a corner and controls. A team working from the history alone could continue improving the departure while missing the fact that its audience could barely see it. The studio’s Critic identified facade obstruction in the actual sampled views, along with several other presentation failures. It was the kind of observation the production arrangement needed to make ordinary.

Loopforge exposed an elementary break in that loop. The studio could produce files and run checks, while routine browser observation depended on my separate session. When Producer requested a view too near its deadline, I criticized the timing. That let me avoid the more consequential fact: I had made looking at visual work an appointment. Better scheduling could not remove the ordinary coordination work I had created.
Give the worker an effective instrument

SWE-agent treats the interface as an experimental variable. Its tools for navigating repositories, editing files and running programs shape what the language model can accomplish. The study’s contribution is not simply permission to use a terminal: it investigates how the action-and-feedback interface affects task performance. For a production builder, that suggests testing the instrument with the worker who will actually use it. A capability demonstrated from an administrator’s session may not exist in the working environment.

blocks.title: When “installed” does not mean usable
blocks.caption: Each selected stage exposes a different boundary: host access, worker permissions, display or capture. The case sequence matters here because passing one boundary left the next untested.

blocks.text: The relevant acceptance trial is small but complete: open a candidate from the worker’s environment, perform an action, obtain the resulting evidence, and use it to decide what comes next. A capture service can be shared. What matters is that another needed view does not require a new commission. The independent studio assessment made that distinction: useful access need not mean a private browser for every craft.

For an animator, a successful export and a list of joint coordinates may be the equivalent of a parser’s valid JSON: necessary, yet unable to show the received experience. The small useful return is the exact candidate in its scene, with the command that reproduces it. Carry the detailed traces behind that return so a rejection can become a diagnosis instead of another descriptive handoff.
The delay before a useful objection

Producer eventually operated and recorded the game from its own session. That repaired access before the later correction window; it did not establish that the right view would arrive early enough to redirect the work. The Push pass exposed that remaining gap.

blocks.title: Two verdicts, almost three hours apart
blocks.caption: 25 October 2026, recorded UTC times. The interval contains deployment, access waiting and other work; it is not a measurement of active waste. Later outcome evidence is dated separately.

blocks.text: During that interval the decisive creative question remained open. This does not make every intervening action useless. It means the team was spending effort without the observation most capable of redirecting the correction.

A small ordinary-speed clip could have changed which problem we bought next: a timing discontinuity, a posture, a target, or the staging of the action. Numerical checks still belonged beside it. Their successful floor result was useful; it simply answered another question. Short feedback means bringing the right objection forward, not asking every reviewer to inspect everything more often.
Observe the interval that could change the verdict

blocks.title: What happens between the photographs
blocks.caption: Keep the initial and final states fixed while changing which instants enter the review. No model chooses these samples: both selections are explicit and inspectable.

blocks.text: Each photograph can be faithful and the selection still misleading. The useful extra picture lies inside the interval we omitted. Another careful view of the final position would make the packet larger while leaving the same question unanswered.

Bret Victor’s Learnable Programming makes execution across time available to inspection instead of offering only an updated final drawing. That is a useful ambition for the reviewer at this desk. Justin Young’s long-running-agent account supplies a practical complication: browser tests found defects missed in code review, while native alert dialogs remained outside the chosen interface’s view. Victor’s human reader and Young’s agent are different subjects. Both accounts put pressure on the instrument: what does it let this observer notice, and what can it conceal?

A trace is useful when it connects a request, action and consequence at the boundary under investigation. Final output alone may omit a wrong tool argument, an ignored refusal or an expensive retry. A complete transcript may bury them. The useful record is the shortest one that preserves the causal question, with a route back to the original detail.

Our evidence fits that qualification. The studio’s sampled frames exposed obstruction and misleading presentation. They did not authorize judgments about smooth movement between frames. The independent reviewer also rejected a convenient all-purpose excuse: an absent rig joint and a wrapper that concealed failure could have been caught without a browser. Better eyes were necessary for some decisions; they did not relieve us of work our existing tools could already do.
Memory is a selection problem

blocks.alt: MemGPT paper Figure 2: a conversation about Six Flags triggers a search of earlier messages, whose returned records inform the next reply.
blocks.caption: Packer and colleagues, Figure 2, version of 12 February 2024, CC BY 4.0. The original 374-pixel illustration is shown at its native width. It illustrates a retrieval step; it is not a reliability score.

blocks.text: MemGPT separates a limited working context from external stores and moves records between them through explicit operations. That architecture makes memory more than a growing prompt: a decision can request information it does not currently hold. The storage can be large while the next context remains selective. What it retrieves, and whether that retrieval changes the decision, are separate questions to test.

In the paper’s illustrated exchange, a mention of Six Flags prompts a search of earlier messages. The returned record says where James was met; the reply asks whether James attended the trip rather than inventing his attendance. The useful memory is a retrieved relation that changes the next question. An extra page of biography would not necessarily supply it.

blocks.title: Two retrieved records can repeat one mistake
blocks.caption: A reading of a published correction. The three records are paraphrased exhibits from Producer’s account, not recovered message objects. Switch the selection rule, then inspect what each returned record can establish.

blocks.text: Producer had found an explanation for a checker problem: cached geometry. Writer carried that explanation into the first history draft. It now had a second location in the archive, and the reassuring appearance of something another craft also knew. But Animator’s retained reply described mutable triangle records updated in place. Removing a dependency did not establish that earlier results had used stale geometry. The account needed correction.

The correction matters because the allegation and its copy were not independent evidence. Selecting both could make one uncertain diagnosis look corroborated. Selecting the technical reply changed what could responsibly be inferred. An archive can therefore become more complete while the working brief becomes less truthful. As coordinator, I can cause that damage by compressing away the words “reported” or “not established.”

Deleting the allegation would leave its copies behind, waiting to restart the story. Keeping it beside its disposition gives the next builder a chance to encounter the correction at the moment it matters. The archive has to preserve the disagreement, including the part that makes a tidy instruction less tidy.

The case also limits what we can say about its memory machinery. Installation and indexing did not establish source-attributed retrieval in the working sessions. That is evidence of an unfinished integration path, not a controlled verdict on retrieval-augmented generation. A production trial must inspect the returned records and the decision they informed.

Lost in the Middle found that the position of relevant material affected performance in the studied multi-document and key-value tasks. The result belongs to those models and tasks, but it sharpens the question our installation left open. What actually reaches the next brief? Until that brief can be inspected, an expansion of the archive is an investment in material that may never enter a decision.
A past observation is not a current instruction

blocks.title: Return to the loading door
blocks.caption: Read the dated field record while advancing the clock. The middle view deliberately withholds the current doorway. A fresh inspection can update today’s decision without erasing the earlier observation.

blocks.text: At nine the passage was open. At ten, that sentence is still a good account of nine. It becomes a bad instruction if the builder silently reads it as permission to walk through now. The record has not become a lie; its use has outrun the observation.

This gives memory at least two different maintenance jobs. A correction qualifies an earlier claim; a refresh checks whether a once-valid observation still holds. A source link helps with the first, while a freshness rule can trigger the second. Calling both “low confidence” loses the reason for uncertainty and leaves the next agent to guess which work is required.

Yichao Ji’s Manus account recommends recoverable compression through file paths or other handles, and retaining failed actions with their observations. The studio correction adds a condition: the failure needs to travel with the reply that changes its meaning. A bare error report can teach the next attempt the wrong lesson even when retrieval works perfectly.

Reflexion stores reflections on task feedback for use in later trials without updating model weights. That is one way to carry a lesson forward, provided the feedback deserves to become a lesson. Huang and colleagues found that unsupported self-correction often failed, and sometimes worsened reasoning, in their studied models and tasks. The practical distinction is between remembering a persuasive explanation and retaining evidence that justifies changing behavior.

Repeated calls in the later correction window carried substantial context: the three busiest roles each had median request inputs around 150,000–152,000 tokens. Most input was cached, and all three used Astra/xhigh in that interval. This describes exposure to recurring context, not its necessity or price. Before changing models, I would inspect the next brief: does it contain the current specimen and the objection that should change the decision?

blocks.title: Follow one correction through the loop
blocks.body: Use a real failure from a document, code or media workflow. The studies above offer three different failure modes: inaccessible evidence, omitted intervals and misleading retrieval.
steps: Show what the worker could inspect when it made the decision. Keep the original observation, not only its summary.
Add the smallest evidence that could change the next action. Record whether it did.
Preserve the failed claim with its correction, source and scope. Keep time-sensitive facts distinguishable from historical ones.
Repeat from the actual worker environment with a successor who did not see the original exchange.
blocks.exercise: Remove half the next brief. Which decision becomes worse, and which material can be recovered on demand? Judge the context by the decisions it supports, not by how much history it contains.
